title: Postmortem: a one-image request billed 10 images
description: Hubu authorized two Gemini 3 Pro Image edits for $0.27 and Google billed $1.92 for 14 images. What happened, why the cost check came too late, what we learned about Gemini image billing, and what is changing.

cover.alt: Hubu incident postmortem cover with the title A one-image request billed 10 images and the subtitle Authorized $0.27, billed $1.92. A table shows the patch request asked for 1 image, returned 4 and billed $0.55; the sticker request asked for 1, returned 10 and billed $1.37; in total 2 asked, 14 returned, $1.92 billed, about a 7 times overrun.

title: From Rust adapters to provider packs
description: Why Hubu replaced hand-written Rust provider adapters with TOML provider packs run by reviewed engines, how the migration went, and how it sets up adding providers from a web UI.

cover.alt: Hubu article cover with the title From Rust adapters to provider packs and the subtitle New providers as data, not code. A panel lists packs/verified/: flux2_api.rs struck through as deleted, 3,681 lines; bfl-flux-3-image.toml as a pack on async_poll; and a Google Gemini v2 pack on sync_fixed.

title: Why AI agents need a call ID before they spend money
description: Why Hubu takes a trusted per-call ID from the agent harness, never the tool's arguments, and turns it into the idempotency key that prevents double spend.

cover.alt: Hubu article cover with the title Why AI agents need a call ID before they spend money. A panel maps call IDs to operations: call_7f3a maps to op A, charged once; the same call_7f3a on retry maps to op A again, replayed with no new charge; a new call_9c1e maps to op B with a new charge.

title: Budgets that keep up with agents
description: A preview of the accounting precision work underway for Hubu v0.2.4, and why sub-cent agent spending makes it important now.

cover.alt: Hubu article cover: a budget moves from coarse cent divisions to precise micro-dollar divisions, with the title Budgets that keep up with agents.
